dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: May the Anemo Archon guide the expedition on its path...

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: Before Anselm comes back, this place could do with a good tidying up...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The expedition?

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: Yes. My husband, Anselm, he's currently away. He followed Grand Master Varka on the expedition.

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: He mentioned in his letters that he's been promoted to deputy after Cardinal Seamus was transferred...

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: I should be proud, but when I think about Nod-Krai, with all the disasters there, my heart just won't settle... He's only in charge of logistics. If something happens, if monsters appear... how is he meant to protect himself?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: May the Anemo Archon bless him.

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: Thank you. May the Anemo Archon protect you on your journey as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: Hehe, this? This is a battle too! The battle of cleaning!

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: Since the expedition team switched to a rotation schedule, that rascal man of mine finally gets to come home more often.

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: It might only be a quick visit, but I can't let him walk into a messy house.

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: If he spots dust on the windowsill, he'll probably start nagging me like he's drilling new recruits at camp.

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: Hmph. And if he dares lecture me, I'll make him sleep on the floor.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: Take care! You're welcome here anytime.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You can count on the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: *sigh* I trust the Knights. Truly, I do. I just don't have any faith in Anselm's scrawny constitution.

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: Every household has its own worries, doesn't it? Take the neighbors next door, for example. No one in their family went on the expedition, and yet they're still constantly fretting over their daughter.

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: Their daughter... Mona, I believe? I hear she's renting a place in Mondstadt now, making a living reading fortunes for people.

dialogues.speaker: Rosenthal
dialogues.text: Her family's well-off, too, but she still refuses to live with her parents. Always on the move, always busy... Different strokes for different folks, as they say.
